properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 21 at 11:21AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
Elevated fire weather conditions can be expected across portions
of southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi this afternoon.
Relative humidity values are forecast to drop into the 25 to 35
percent range. The 20 ft wind forecast is at or less than 10 mph,
which will limit critical fire weather conditions or at least the
effective spread of fires that may ignite.

Numerous local burn bans remain in place across LA and MS due to
ongoing drought conditions. This includes East Feliciana, St.
Helena, Tangipahoa, and Washington Parishes along with Wilkinson,
Amite, and Pike Counties. Regardless, outdoor burning is strongly
not recommended this afternoon, and all local restrictions
followed.

Additional statements, Fire Weather Watches or Red Flag Warnings
will be possible in the upcoming days as drought conditions
worsen, relative humidity values remain low during the afternoon,
and eventually winds begin to increase, especially this weekend.

NWSheadline: ELEVATED FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS THIS AFTERNOON

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 21 at 10:08AM MDT until October 23 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southwest New Mexico, including the following
areas, Central Grant County/Silver City Area, Southern Gila Region
Highlands/Black Range and Upper Gila River Valley.

* WHEN...From Thursday afternoon through early Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An incoming potent upper level system coupled with abnormally
high moisture will allow for scattered to numerous thunderstorms
Thursday afternoon, evening and into Friday morning. Storms will
be efficient rain makers which could lead to flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Watch issued October 21 at 10:06AM MDT until October 23 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Boise ID
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
are possible over the Crooked burn scar and Wapiti burn scar. Total
rainfall up to 1.25 inch is possible on the burn scars.

* WHERE...Wapiti and Crooked burn scars in southwest Idaho.

* WHEN...From Thursday evening through Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Crooked and Wapiti burn scars is
expected up to and during the period of the watch. Residents near
the Crooked and Wapiti burn scar should prepare for potential
debris flow. Be sure to stay up to date with information from local
authorities. Heavy rainfall could trigger flash flooding or debris
flows in and near recent wildfire burn scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting heavy
rainfall over the Crooked and Wapiti burn scar, which may lead to
flash flooding and debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Grandjean and Barber Flat Guard Station.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 21 at 10:11AM AST until October 21 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...Exposed northwesterly and north-facing beaches of
Puerto Rico, Culebra, and the northern US Virgin Islands.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.
